question.problem: Consider two random variables $X$ and $Y$ with expectations $\text{E}[X]=1,$ $\text{E}[Y]=3,$ mixed moment $\text{E}[XY]=2,$ and second raw moments $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=2$ and $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]=15.$ Find the variance of $4X+3Y.$

current_example.problem:
The joint probability mass function of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.2$ |

Find $\textrm{Var}[5X+2Y].$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\textrm{Var}[aX+bY] = a^2 \textrm{Var}[X] + b^2 \textrm{Var}[Y] + 2ab\,\textrm{Cov}[X,Y].
$$

Also, the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm{E}[X^2] - \textrm{E}[X]^2,
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\textrm{Cov}[X,Y] = \textrm{E}[XY] - \textrm{E}[X] \cdot \textrm{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $f_X$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ |
| $f_Y$ | $0.5$ | $0.5$ | $1$ |

Now, we can find $\textrm{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space $S_X,$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.4+3\cdot 0.6 \\  & =1.8\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & ={0}^{2}\cdot 0.4+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.6 \\  & =5.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =5.4-{1.8}^{2} \\  & =2.16.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space $S_Y,$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =0\cdot 0.5+2\cdot 0.5 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}{y}^{2}\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & ={0}^{2}\cdot 0.5+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.5 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =2-{1}^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's find $\textrm{Cov}[X,Y].$ We find $\textrm{E}[XY]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =0\cdot 0\cdot f(0,0)+0\cdot 2\cdot f(0,2)+3\cdot 0\cdot f(3,0)+3\cdot 2\cdot f(3,2) \\  & =0+0+0+6\cdot 0.2 \\  & =1.2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[XY] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =1.2-1.8\cdot 1 \\  & =-0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[5X+2Y] & ={5}^{2}\cdot 2.16+{2}^{2}\cdot 1+2\cdot 5\cdot 2\cdot (-0.6) \\  & =54+4-12 \\  & =46.\end{aligned}
$$
